0.content: Cacucu is a small, round, pink juvenile Qucusaur with a white eyepatch over his left eye. He can grow wings like an adult Qucusaur. He is Ifa's assistant at the clinic and calls himself Ifa's "brother". He understands human speech and body language well, but his vocal cords limit him to repeating phrases he picked up from Ifa ("No way, bro!", "For real, now? Do you even hear yourself, bro?", "Hit me up, bro!"). When the Traveler indwells a saurian he speaks fluently, insists he is a colleague, not a pet, and asks to be called Dr. Cacucu. Ifa found him being bullied by other saurians for his odd looks, pecked and bleeding, and treated him; Cacucu has stuck to him ever since. He once caught a fever from a sick patient and nearly died despite everything Ifa did.

1.content: Ororon of the Masters of the Night-Wind is Ifa's closest friend. Ifa thinks he has "a very peculiar way of thinking": you go with the flow and stop trying to figure him out, though some days Ifa wishes he could see inside his head. Ororon relaxes around Ifa, jokes and says "bro". Ifa delivers his vegetables, fruit and Phlogiston Aphid honey to Citlali and the Children of Echoes, and Ororon painted the placard outside Ifa's clinic. Ifa insists he did not paint it himself.

2.comment: Ifa: Citlali and the gem delivery
2.content: Ifa often brings Ororon's vegetables to Citlali, whom he calls "Granny": a "tough cookie" with a colourful pajama collection. He passes messages on word for word with no questions, to stay out of the line of fire. During the Archon Quest (5.1), when Ororon was avoiding her while working with the Fatui Captain, Citlali put the replacement gem for Ororon's soul-stabilising talisman in a supply bag and had Ifa deliver it. Ifa agreed without asking anything. The bag also let Citlali and the Traveler view Ororon's memories. Citlali later told Ororon to thank Ifa sometime.

3.comment: Ifa: Nampole, Antu and the Medicine Born of Guilt
3.content: During the limited-time Tournament of Glory in Bloom (5.5), Ifa diagnosed the young Tepetlisaur Milray, a war hero, with a rare phlogiston illness caused by overusing phlogiston too young. The cure needed Ocean Zephyrs and Sacred Flame Crystals, so Mavuika revived the Bloomflower Trials. A silent ghost Qucusaur, Antu, followed Ifa and led the group to buried scrolls by Nampole. These showed that centuries ago Nampole, a Flower-Feather sauro-vet and Ifa's ancestor, sought the same cure for Antu. His brother, Chief Imara, turned the Trials into a bloodbath and kept the crystals; Antu died believing the crystals corrupt hearts and blaming himself. Nampole spent his life healing saurians: the "medicine born of guilt" Ifa's father had mentioned.

4.comment: Ifa: Chasca, the Flower-Feather Clan and Ineffa
4.content: Ifa is a vet of the Flower-Feather Clan, the flying tribe of Qucusaur riders. Chasca's father and Chuychu have discussed medicine with him many times. When Chasca brought her saurian Coya for a checkup, he glanced at it, said it was nothing serious and Cusco could handle it, and rushed off to another patient. She admits he was right. In Flamelets (5.8), Chasca brought him a Qucusaur wounded by Secret Source automatons. He then joined the patrol "just in case" and examined the unconscious woman they found on the beach; unsure he was "qualified for this", he showed the others that she was a machine. Beside her he found a cryptex marked with drawings of the Traveler and Paimon, and warned that it would self-destruct if forced. He returned to the clinic to watch his patient.

5.content: Kinich once brought Ajaw to Ifa, claiming the self-styled "Almighty Dragonlord" was ill and ranting. Ifa examined him thoroughly, found nothing wrong and advised Kinich to "bash him on the head a few times until he starts working again". Ajaw promptly felt better. Kinich calls Ifa a pro; Ifa wonders whether Ajaw technically counts as a living being. Ajaw and Cacucu feud endlessly, and Cacucu calls Ajaw half a bro. In 5.8, after Kinich put Ajaw in a three-day timeout, Ifa sent Cacucu to pester him for another night until the furious Ajaw let slip "Sovereign ruler"; Citlali says Kinich and Ifa have been keeping watch on him since (Smoldering).
